LESSON: BALAAM’S DONKEY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Holy Bible
Topic 2.3: Balaam’s Donkey

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Balaam’s Donkey. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why did the donkey talk?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. retell the story of Balaam and his donkey,
2. apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions,
3. acquire the value of love by speaking good things about others,
4. acknowledge God’s greatness by revering Him. The learner is guided to: 34, obeying God and their seniors, Donkey, curse or speak ill about others according to Numbers 22:1-6, 20-34, draw the scenarios in this story, Why did the donkey talk?

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. retell the story of Balaam and his donkey,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to retell the story of Balaam and his donkey,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. acquire the value of love by speaking good things about others,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to acquire the value of love by speaking good things about others,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. acknowledge God’s greatness by revering Him. The learner is guided to: 34, obeying God and their seniors, Donkey, curse or speak ill about others according to Numbers 22:1-6, 20-34, draw the scenarios in this story, Why did the donkey talk?
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to acknowledge God’s greatness by revering Him. The learner is guided to: 34, obeying God and their seniors, Donkey, curse or speak ill about others according to Numbers 22:1-6, 20-34, draw the scenarios in this story, Why did the donkey talk?. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Balaam’s Donkey.
2. Explain Balaam’s Donkey to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: in groups, read Numbers 22:1-6, 20- 34,
4. Show that you can: retell the story of Balaam and his donkey,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Balaam’s Donkey. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why did the donkey talk?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. In groups, read Numbers 22:1-6, 20- 34,
2. In pairs, list the importance of obeying God and their seniors,

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. retell the story of Balaam and his donkey,
2. apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions,
3. acquire the value of love by speaking good things about others,
4. acknowledge God’s greatness by revering Him. The learner is guided to: 34, obeying God and their seniors, Donkey, curse or speak ill about others according to Numbers 22:1-6, 20-34, draw the scenarios in this story, Why did the donkey talk?

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
